questions.text: When I disagree with someone, my reaction is...

options.text: Press logically to get my point across.
Avoid the situation for now and wait for emotions to cool.
Give up my opinion to avoid hurting their feelings.
Suggest a point where both can compromise slightly.
Take time to find an alternative that satisfies both.

questions.text: In a conflict, what I value most is...

options.text: Solving the problem accurately and winning
Reducing psychic energy consumption
Maintaining the relationship with the other person
Ending inefficient consumption and compromising
Growth opportunity to deeply understand each other's needs
Express my intentions firmly and strongly.
Shut up and leave the place.
Apologize first to calm their anger.
Try to finish roughly at some point.
Try to talk about why I am angry.

questions.text: When opinions differ in a team project, I...

options.text: Persuade others to adopt my idea.
Just follow the direction the majority wants.
Choose team peace even if I suffer a loss.
Suggest mixing each other's opinions half and half.
Propose finding a third way everyone can agree on.

questions.text: How do I feel after resolving a conflict?

options.text: A sense of victory that things went my way.
Relieved that it just ended quickly.
Happy that the other person is grateful.
Think we divided things fairly.
Feeling closer by solving the problem together.

questions.text: When someone makes an unreasonable request?

options.text: Flatly say no.
Heard it but delay answering and avoid it.
Accept it for the sake of goodness.
Suggest doing something else instead.
Ask the fundamental reason for making such a request.

questions.text: If someone bursts into tears during an argument?

options.text: Continue saying emotion and logic are separate.
Don't know what to do and leave immediately.
Apologize immediately and cater to their mood.
Tell them to calm down and talk again tomorrow.
Stop the conversation and empathize with their sadness.

questions.text: When there is a difference in important values?

options.text: Try to prove I am right until the end.
Stop the discussion saying what can we do if we are different.
Respect their values and adjust myself.
Draw a line of mutual respect and agree.
Create a larger framework where both values can coexist.
Point it out immediately and demand correction.
Pretend not to know to prevent conflict.
Fix it myself so they don't lose face.
Tell them I'll fix this part, so you do that part.
Check the process behind the mistake together and find alternatives.
Counterattack by pointing out their faults even more.
Cut off contact or ignore them.
Say sorry unconditionally for now.
Sorry for the disappointment, but I had my own reasons.
Ask for the true feelings hidden behind the criticism.

questions.text: To someone who is late for an appointment?

options.text: Strongly admonish them on the importance of punctuality.
Feel bad but just eat without saying anything.
Smile and say it's fine, they must have been busy.
Tell them they should also have time waiting later.
Listen to why they were late and think of solutions together.

questions.text: When a value you can never give up is challenged?

options.text: Choose to give up the relationship rather than my values.
Avoid the discussion itself and hide my thoughts.
Accept their values and try to modify my thoughts.
Leave only the core and concede the rest.
Find a high-level consensus where my values and theirs harmonize.

accommodating.title: Sacrificial Accommodator
accommodating.description: Pursues harmony by putting others' needs before their own.
accommodating.advice: Your hurt heart is also a precious asset to care for.
accommodating.resonanceImpact: Soft resonance that flexibly deforms oneself to match others.

avoiding.title: Silent Pacifist
avoiding.description: Tends to avoid conflict itself and preserve energy.
avoiding.advice: Sometimes honest conversation resolves problems faster than silence.
avoiding.resonanceImpact: Freezes conflict by stopping vibrations, but unresolved grudges remain.

collaborating.title: Resonating Creator
collaborating.description: A style that creates a third alternative where everyone can win-win.
collaborating.advice: Efforts to find the best answer in every conflict can sometimes exhaust you.
collaborating.resonanceImpact: Amplifying resonance that merges two different vibrations to create greater harmony.

competing.title: Firm Competitor
competing.description: A style that exerts strong drive to achieve their goals.
competing.advice: Remember that victory is not always more important than peace in relationships.
competing.resonanceImpact: A resonance that gives intense drive but may cause alienation for the other.

compromising.title: Practical Negotiator
compromising.description: Skilled at finding an appropriate middle ground by each conceding a bit.
compromising.advice: Think about fundamental solutions, not just temporary agreements.
compromising.resonanceImpact: Stable resonance that finds an appropriate compromise by adjusting frequencies.
